headline: Computational methods for immune receptor pairing and tumor-reactive T cell detection
label: Single Cell Immune Profiling Methods
summary: Single-cell and spatial platforms now resolve receptor pairing, tumor-reactive T cells, and multi-study tissue atlases at cellular resolution.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how computational and platform choices determine which cellular and receptor-level information is recovered from single-cell and spatial data. SPaCeD pairs heavy and light B cell receptor chains from spatial BCR-seq by combining expression matrices with optimal-transport spatial distances. Turep applies deep learning with generative augmentation to predict tumor-reactive T cells across cancers from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. A unified HNSCC scRNA-seq atlas of 78 patients (274,911 cells) harmonizes studies via STACAS integration and Ikarus/scGate annotation to address HPV- and sex-associated microenvironment variability. Benchmarking of 10x and Parse on matched PBMCs evaluates transcriptome quality and TCR chain recovery, and the IBD spatial atlas benchmarks CosMx against Xenium. The set is heterogeneous: only the first two items are modeling methods, while the benchmarking and platform comparisons concern technology effects rather than tumor biology. The newer element is methodological, with receptor pairing, tumor-reactivity prediction, and cross-study harmonization each addressed through explicit computational design.
